definitions.explanation: Earrings designed to go through pierced ears.
The hole or piercing itself in the ear.

examples.japanese: ⟦{誕生日|たんじょうび}→誕生日：02910_tanjoubi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ピアス⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I received earrings for my birthday.

examples.japanese: ⟦{金|きん}→金：02666_kin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ピアス⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけている→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧。
⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦おそろい→お揃い：27779_osoroi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ピアス⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}って→買う：00489_kau⟧、⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦つけている→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧。

examples.english: I had my ears pierced at a clinic, so I felt at ease.

notes:
ピアス comes from English 'pierce' and has a specific meaning in Japanese that differs from English usage.

IMPORTANT DISTINCTION:
- ピアス: Earrings for pierced ears / the piercing itself
- ⟦イヤリング→イヤリング：04684_iyaringu⟧: Clip-on earrings (no piercing)

In English, 'earring' is the general term, but in Japanese, these are distinct categories.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ピアス⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧ (to put on earrings)
- ピアス⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ (to get ears pierced)
- ピアス⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{穴|あな}→穴：01691_ana⟧ (piercing hole)
- ピアス⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{外|はず}す→外す：02394_hazusu⟧ (to remove earrings)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many Japanese schools and workplaces prohibit or restrict ピアス. Some people get their ears pierced at ⟦{皮膚科|ひふか}→皮膚科：11073_hifuka⟧ (dermatology clinic) for safety.
